title: Keep the £2 bus fare cap running beyond 2027
headline: The cap is funded to December 2027. This keeps it: £400m a year.
description: Single bus fares in England outside London are capped at £2 from 1 January to 31 December 2027, backed by £400m of government funding. The cap ends with the year unless a Budget extends it. This lever extends it indefinitely from January 2028 at the government's own figure for a year of the cap: £400m, a quarter of which falls in 2027-28 and the rest in each year after.

baselinePolicy.text: The £2 cap for calendar year 2027 is government policy, funded from the energy department's budget by switching international climate finance from grants to loans. Nothing in the baseline funds it beyond 31 December 2027.

source.quote: single bus tickets will be capped at £2 in England outside London from 1 January until 31 December 2027
The new £2 cap is backed by £400 million of extra government funding.

terms.label: Cost of a full year of the cap

source.quote: backed by £400 million of extra government funding

terms.label: Years of cap this extension adds, from 1 January 2028

source.note: The funded cap runs to 31 December 2027, so the extension covers nothing before 2027-28 and the first quarter of 2028 falls in 2027-28.

rawSource.note: The government's own cost of a year's cap, times the part of each fiscal year the extension covers. Held flat in cash: a rising fare gap would cost more, and nothing published says how much.

caveats: £400m is the government's figure for the 2027 cap. Fares, ridership and the fare gap the cap has to bridge all move, and this holds the figure flat in cash.
The cap applies in England outside London; extending it is an English decision with Barnett consequentials.

considerations.text: The 2027 cap was paid for inside the energy department's budget, by switching international climate finance from grants to loans. An extension has no such offset written down, so it is new spending unless a Budget finds another.

sources.quote: funded by savings from reprioritising the Department for Energy Security and Net Zero's budget, including by switching funding for international climate from grants to loans

considerations.text: Bus policy is devolved. An English cap generates Barnett consequentials for Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland on top of the figure shown.
